Diagnosis.submission:
Root cause: Platform automation halved the frontend workload's CPU ceiling (limits.cpu 1 -> 500m, request raised to match) about seven minutes before onset [tr_ec5e968a606a]. The edit recreated the pod: a full cold-start sequence appears at 21:10:11, one second after the change, with all five downstream gRPC clients connecting cleanly [tr_44133780e673]. From that point the frontend goes quiet — no further log output [tr_44133780e673], zero error spans across 22 samples [tr_a1e1555af34a, tr_d2052c256486], and three intervals with no spans at all, meaning it served nothing in those intervals [tr_a1e1555af34a, tr_d2052c256486]. That is CPU starvation under the new ceiling: requests stall rather than fail, so callers hang while the frontend reports no errors. The limit edit is how it started; exhaustion is the failing mechanism.
Faulty component: frontend
Fault type: resource_exhaustion
Confidence: medium

Evidence:
- A resource-limits change landed on the frontend workload about 7 minutes before onset, cutting the CPU limit by half and raising the CPU request to equal the new limit, applied by platform automation. (found, from change_history on frontend)
- The frontend Service object and its container workload were first created roughly 9 minutes before onset, indicating this frontend instance was newly stood up immediately prior to the incident rather than long-running. (found, from change_history on frontend)
- All three recorded changes originate from the same automated actor; there is no evidence of a human-initiated deploy, config push, or feature-flag flip in the window. (found, from change_history on frontend)
- A code deploy or new application image on frontend introduced the regression. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: The only frontend changes in the window are the initial workload/Service creation and a resource-limits edit; no image or application version change is recorded.)
- A feature-flag flip toggled behaviour just before onset. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: No flag-flip entries appear among the three frontend changes in the window.)
- The change landed too long before onset to be causally related, so the trigger is unrelated to change activity. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: The resource-limits edit lands 7 minutes before onset, tight enough to remain a live candidate rather than being timed out.)
- Nothing changed on frontend and the fault must be purely environmental or load-driven. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: Three changes are recorded on frontend inside the window, including a CPU ceiling reduction.)
- The only error-level lines frontend emitted in the queried 30-minute window are nine identical SearchHandler CheckAvailability failures, all stamped at a single second, 21:10:03 — roughly seven minutes before the 21:17:39 time of interest, not around it. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Eight seconds after that error burst, at 21:10:11, the frontend emitted a complete cold-start sequence (config read, Jaeger agent init, Consul agent init, gRPC client initialization, then serving HTTP), indicating the pod restarted immediately following the error cluster. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- On restart the frontend successfully established gRPC connections to all five downstream dependencies it initializes (search, profile, recommendation, user, reservation) and reached the serving state without further error output. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The failing call path is the frontend's outbound availability check on the search handler, so the error is a symptom of a downstream dependency response rather than an internal frontend fault; the log line itself carries no status code or peer address to identify which dependency. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})

Reasoning:
The only substantive change in the window is a CPU ceiling cut on the frontend itself; no image, version or flag change exists [tr_ec5e968a606a]. The restart timestamp matches the edit to the second and shows healthy service discovery and five successful downstream connections [tr_44133780e673], which argues against a wrong address, credential or dependency as the mechanism. The post-restart signature is absence rather than failure: flat-zero error ratio with zero variance plus intervals containing no spans at all [tr_a1e1555af34a, tr_d2052c256486] and silent logs [tr_44133780e673] — work not completing while nothing errors is what throttling looks like from outside the container. The downstream story is weak: the nine CheckAvailability failures are a single-second burst at 21:10:03, before the alert, and never recur [tr_44133780e673], while reservation logged no CheckAvailability activity at all [tr_eacfd29a4cab]. Traces could have arbitrated but returned nothing for frontend across the whole window including the healthy period, so the trace path is itself impaired [tr_adf228881c31]. The fix is restoring the previous CPU limit.

Alternatives considered:
1. frontend: The frontend telemetry pipeline is broken and the apparent outage is an observability gap rather than a service fault. (unknown). Ranked lower because: It does not explain the alert at 21:17:39, and a concrete CPU-limit cut landing seven minutes before onset is a better fit than instrument failure [tr_ec5e968a606a].
2. search: A downstream dependency behind the search/availability path became slow, and the frontend hung waiting on it. (dependency_latency). Ranked lower because: The only evidence is a single-second error burst before onset that never recurs [tr_44133780e673]; no trace or metric data identifies a slow downstream, and reservation's logs are empty [tr_eacfd29a4cab, tr_adf228881c31].

Open questions:
- No container-level data was ever returned — CPU throttling ratio, restart counts and OOM/eviction events were requested but absent [tr_d2052c256486]; throttling is inferred, not measured.
- Why frontend traces are missing for the entire window including the pre-incident baseline, and why a zero-result query was flagged truncated [tr_adf228881c31] — a broken telemetry pipeline would undermine the 'no spans means no traffic' inference.
- What the 21:10:03 CheckAvailability burst actually hit; the log line carries no peer or status code and reservation's logs are empty under that filter [tr_44133780e673, tr_eacfd29a4cab].
